quotes.text: Data Verse is not just another list. It's built as a database layer for the power platform, not a prettier share point table.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear definition of what Dataverse is compared to SharePoint lists.

quotes.text: Seen another way, data verse front loads it's pain. You spend money and effort upfront. Lists backload their pain. You spend nothing today, but you leak time for years.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable trade-off between upfront cost and long-term technical debt.

quotes.text: Trials are temporary and not every license covers production use. Don't assume those trial checkboxes equal long term rights. Validate your licenses with procurement before you migrate a single workload.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical licensing warning before a Dataverse rollout.

quotes.text: Copilot doesn't understand your business rules, and it won't know why finance data shouldn't link the way marketing wants it to. Treat it like a helper in the room, not the architect of the house.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced view of AI assistance in data modeling.

quotes.text: Migration feels a lot closer to re architecture than to copypaste. If you run it like a file copy, you'll spend weeks fixing fall out.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets the right expectation for list-to-Dataverse migrations.

takeaways: Use SharePoint lists for small, short-term needs and Dataverse when you need relationships, record-level security, auditing and scale.
Budget Dataverse like infrastructure: validate licensing and premium features with procurement and plan storage, schema, roles and skills upfront.
Treat a list-to-Dataverse migration as re-architecture with an inventory, data cleanup, rebuilt security roles and flows, a pilot and a rollback plan.
hook: Your SharePoint list tracker has outgrown its duct tape, but Dataverse brings licensing, storage and skills costs. This episode is for Power Platform makers and IT leads deciding between lists, Dataverse and SQL, with a simple gut check, a budgeting checklist and a migration plan that avoids broken flows and security surprises.
